Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 6, "heading": "CHAPTER 4. I FALL INTO DISGRACE", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u006-b0084", "target": "С расстояния времени мне кажется, что мои несчастные занятия обычно шли именно так. Я мог бы очень хорошо учиться, не будь рядом Мэрдстонов; но влияние Мэрдстонов на меня было подобно завораживающему действию двух змей на несчастную молодую птицу. Даже когда мне удавалось пережить утро с сносной репутацией, выигрывал я немного — только обед; ибо мисс Мэрдстон никак не могла терпеть, чтобы я оставался без дела, и, если я неосторожно выказывал праздность, привлекала внимание брата ко мне словами: «Клара, дорогая, нет ничего лучше труда — дайте вашему мальчику упражнение»; из-за чего меня тут же усаживали за какую-нибудь новую работу. Что до каких-либо развлечений с другими детьми моего возраста, то их у меня было совсем мало: мрачное богословие Мэрдстонов выставляло всех детей скопищем маленьких гадюк (хотя ведь БЫЛ же когда-то ребёнок, поставленный посреди учеников) и полагало, что они заражают друг друга.", "source_sha256": "f13a27cefd1985886c5175d6981f023a7971b1f57084d5484fb1163da4623f62", "target_id": "ru-en85-u006-b0084", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "7988f5ce12dda90e2aa398812ccc3023d6cfa59b4b8040a372a1bf39dc654ca0"}, {"source_id": "en85-u006-b0085", "target": "Естественным результатом такого обращения, продолжавшегося, полагаю, около шести месяцев или больше, было то, что я стал угрюмым, тупым и упрямым. Тем более таким меня делало ощущение, что с каждым днём я всё больше отстранён и отчуждён от матери. Думаю, я почти отупел бы совсем, если бы не одно обстоятельство.", "source_sha256": "27a0a3dfaf5cbc70d8109f0cf8384e4963430ac737ef110ab29f6fb0a52cc82f", "target_id": "ru-en85-u006-b0085", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "b82cf21db5cb56e510fe2db257fe74da14090536489ea034bbe50e001f16c0f0"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 4, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u006-b0086", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It was this. My father had left a small collection of books in a little room upstairs, to which I had access (for it adjoined my own) and which nobody else in our house ever troubled. From that blessed little room, Roderick Random, Peregrine Pickle, Humphrey Clinker, Tom Jones, the Vicar of Wakefield, Don Quixote, Gil Blas, and Robinson Crusoe, came out, a glorious host, to keep me company. They kept alive my fancy, and my hope of something beyond that place and time,—they, and the Arabian Nights, and the Tales of the Genii,—and did me no harm; for whatever harm was in some of them was not there for me; I knew nothing of it. It is astonishing to me now, how I found time, in the midst of my porings and blunderings over heavier themes, to read those books as I did. It is curious to me how I could ever have consoled myself under my small troubles (which were great troubles to me), by impersonating my favourite characters in them—as I did—and by putting Mr. and Miss Murdstone into all the bad ones—which I did too. I have been Tom Jones (a child’s Tom Jones, a harmless creature) for a week together. I have sustained my own idea of Roderick Random for a month at a stretch, I verily believe. I had a greedy relish for a few volumes of Voyages and Travels—I forget what, now—that were on those shelves; and for days and days I can remember to have gone about my region of our house, armed with the centre-piece out of an old set of boot-trees—the perfect realization of Captain Somebody, of the Royal British Navy, in danger of being beset by savages, and resolved to sell his life at a great price. The Captain never lost dignity, from having his ears boxed with the Latin Grammar. I did; but the Captain was a Captain and a hero, in despite of all the grammars of all the languages in the world, dead or alive.", "sha256": "a45ee252fcb3ba6bd7653d77c78f4347e27f05987fddc2b3f19d444f80b4e884", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[86]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0087", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "This was my only and my constant comfort. When I think of it, the picture always rises in my mind, of a summer evening, the boys at play in the churchyard, and I sitting on my bed, reading as if for life. Every barn in the neighbourhood, every stone in the church, and every foot of the churchyard, had some association of its own, in my mind, connected with these books, and stood for some locality made famous in them. I have seen Tom Pipes go climbing up the church-steeple; I have watched Strap, with the knapsack on his back, stopping to rest himself upon the wicket-gate; and I know that Commodore Trunnion held that club with Mr. Pickle, in the parlour of our little village alehouse.", "sha256": "f191cec02954db3fe21e248b3de63d9468cac4cc655f0fc885ab5ee11a14c298", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[87]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0088", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The reader now understands, as well as I do, what I was when I came to that point of my youthful history to which I am now coming again.", "sha256": "660acb07042d5d7e6adc2d0027ea3907c6b302bbc1d27ba5a6f0fc8e19185d27", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[88]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0089", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "One morning when I went into the parlour with my books, I found my mother looking anxious, Miss Murdstone looking firm, and Mr. Murdstone binding something round the bottom of a cane—a lithe and limber cane, which he left off binding when I came in, and poised and switched in the air.", "sha256": "01b5c9ac98e9df2ae24d5c6ef6ce04beebfa03846aea46bb92e7cff3e5884dc2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[89]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0090", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I tell you, Clara,’ said Mr. Murdstone, ‘I have been often flogged myself.’", "sha256": "f19d2dd7aa224a5dc3489a3d77cc8d2e2ca500b8cf0afae2eab8752a6aaeef64", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[90]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0091", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To be sure; of course,’ said Miss Murdstone.", "sha256": "fede7755d82ba08ec2ee32f4649bd61d872b63efff2c1936c98d03aa47767bdb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[91]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0092", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Certainly, my dear Jane,’ faltered my mother, meekly. ‘But—but do you think it did Edward good?’", "sha256": "213ce75778586d7cbd11dcc53f34809ff79695b30bc4de90b2f8eeb8edbb1509", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[92]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0093", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Do you think it did Edward harm, Clara?’ asked Mr. Murdstone, gravely.", "sha256": "2badfdb96683435337cbe965526edd053283f6e1991968b22d0f965f6e6bd5e9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[93]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0094", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘That’s the point,’ said his sister.", "sha256": "dda0456f2e5cadfc5cbc253f08bb0f02ea14fedf5d27c246fb027c302c5f65bd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[94]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0095", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "To this my mother returned, ‘Certainly, my dear Jane,’ and said no more.", "sha256": "090c4aaab4529579e3a9792f6d9d45beb6e69805ad880894dc01680fcb0211bb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[95]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0096", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I felt apprehensive that I was personally interested in this dialogue, and sought Mr. Murdstone’s eye as it lighted on mine.", "sha256": "a4d9cc8980ec308ebd2b81e903bbe7c6f6a259d3504b48c9008ba8c0d14f0fc3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[96]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0097", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Now, David,’ he said—and I saw that cast again as he said it—‘you must be far more careful today than usual.’ He gave the cane another poise, and another switch; and having finished his preparation of it, laid it down beside him, with an impressive look, and took up his book.", "sha256": "474cfe9a615dfb263dbd623b54b0327b4c8fde2036caa0beb5aeb2b8566431e0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[97]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0098", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "This was a good freshener to my presence of mind, as a beginning. I felt the words of my lessons slipping off, not one by one, or line by line, but by the entire page; I tried to lay hold of them; but they seemed, if I may so express it, to have put skates on, and to skim away from me with a smoothness there was no checking.", "sha256": "01fdbb082c6c1c8e2dae009cc29649f6a2a4aec139698b322c7a24d0d85ee2bc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[98]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0099", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We began badly, and went on worse. I had come in with an idea of distinguishing myself rather, conceiving that I was very well prepared; but it turned out to be quite a mistake. Book after book was added to the heap of failures, Miss Murdstone being firmly watchful of us all the time. And when we came at last to the five thousand cheeses (canes he made it that day, I remember), my mother burst out crying.", "sha256": "c77709a7b44b34d51e5b912879c61cc37334c4af727d69b928d89ab9285b4255", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[99]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0100", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Clara!’ said Miss Murdstone, in her warning voice.", "sha256": "80b6f1bc6191bb7907c5d6fe74c8ef167dd71b055545a9c8237eac74bc933ee2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[100]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0101", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am not quite well, my dear Jane, I think,’ said my mother.", "sha256": "19fd813d89b319100930525afa07f4fba8bef2f8cf765e7dca80fae92122dd29", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[101]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0102", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I saw him wink, solemnly, at his sister, as he rose and said, taking up the cane:", "sha256": "08a533db3d8c64f6c6e5602b6ef0d9f979b8a3fee91bea7c5db79161b8396cf7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[102]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0103", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, Jane, we can hardly expect Clara to bear, with perfect firmness, the worry and torment that David has occasioned her today. That would be stoical. Clara is greatly strengthened and improved, but we can hardly expect so much from her. David, you and I will go upstairs, boy.’", "sha256": "2c2816bfbebfd1719b9c884ba6805983d9a6650e1375b8f3cc4ff48094e23847", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[103]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0104", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As he took me out at the door, my mother ran towards us. Miss Murdstone said, ‘Clara! are you a perfect fool?’ and interfered. I saw my mother stop her ears then, and I heard her crying.", "sha256": "9942b1942fe7e24b10b14ba26c10f928dc3319929b115108a6d9b81e67b6435d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[104]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0105", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He walked me up to my room slowly and gravely—I am certain he had a delight in that formal parade of executing justice—and when we got there, suddenly twisted my head under his arm.", "sha256": "bc131b4ae0ee69fa8621f2098ca07aa744f0f91ccdb72bdbfa6e799cf7789066", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[105]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0106", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Murdstone! Sir!’ I cried to him. ‘Don’t! Pray don’t beat me! I have tried to learn, sir, but I can’t learn while you and Miss Murdstone are by. I can’t indeed!’", "sha256": "07f8728bf74f64250ff7b32349175e6babc168ac198e5ee251ea3b1026605ec8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[106]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0107", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Can’t you, indeed, David?’ he said. ‘We’ll try that.’", "sha256": "6e4d7d7b70b957cf56d2e3e6fd66afb3ad5c7dab4500768c6aac92fcf6fb8999", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[107]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0108", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He had my head as in a vice, but I twined round him somehow, and stopped him for a moment, entreating him not to beat me. It was only a moment that I stopped him, for he cut me heavily an instant afterwards, and in the same instant I caught the hand with which he held me in my mouth, between my teeth, and bit it through. It sets my teeth on edge to think of it.", "sha256": "4d8b39df58d81290e755d1b7ff6294fd5b0a0bd473d81cce09b090d5f01ded55", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[108]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0109", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He beat me then, as if he would have beaten me to death. Above all the noise we made, I heard them running up the stairs, and crying out—I heard my mother crying out—and Peggotty. Then he was gone; and the door was locked outside; and I was lying, fevered and hot, and torn, and sore, and raging in my puny way, upon the floor.", "sha256": "c454369daae28e5bdbc0294fc93c75ce2822801fde6cffcd2923648a70bf42e6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[109]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0110", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "How well I recollect, when I became quiet, what an unnatural stillness seemed to reign through the whole house! How well I remember, when my smart and passion began to cool, how wicked I began to feel!", "sha256": "8616d0a913746fb7724bdb3cd389ca2d4c4096774d538c9841caa614927e3a6f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[110]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0111", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I sat listening for a long while, but there was not a sound. I crawled up from the floor, and saw my face in the glass, so swollen, red, and ugly that it almost frightened me. My stripes were sore and stiff, and made me cry afresh, when I moved; but they were nothing to the guilt I felt. It lay heavier on my breast than if I had been a most atrocious criminal, I dare say.", "sha256": "e4ddeaa4564286d96b103f87171cd66378b72e4fe598868d08b2f8dcc9e83ad8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[111]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0112", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It had begun to grow dark, and I had shut the window (I had been lying, for the most part, with my head upon the sill, by turns crying, dozing, and looking listlessly out), when the key was turned, and Miss Murdstone came in with some bread and meat, and milk. These she put down upon the table without a word, glaring at me the while with exemplary firmness, and then retired, locking the door after her.", "sha256": "fd64dc518fe2dd94cd1e31c668838aec4b2334ab76af704557bc136592c2f552", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[112]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0113", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Long after it was dark I sat there, wondering whether anybody else would come. When this appeared improbable for that night, I undressed, and went to bed; and, there, I began to wonder fearfully what would be done to me. Whether it was a criminal act that I had committed? Whether I should be taken into custody, and sent to prison? Whether I was at all in danger of being hanged?", "sha256": "7ac0c061cbbd4ba96046dcbf2df8dfd951946135fd010f6090a34dbd722199ab", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[113]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0114", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I never shall forget the waking, next morning; the being cheerful and fresh for the first moment, and then the being weighed down by the stale and dismal oppression of remembrance. Miss Murdstone reappeared before I was out of bed; told me, in so many words, that I was free to walk in the garden for half an hour and no longer; and retired, leaving the door open, that I might avail myself of that permission.", "sha256": "3ec16994cacdfe57594d378ad9aae9de5e302cd094d4d549a837d257f4c87c4b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[11]/p[114]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u006-b0115", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I did so, and did so every morning of my imprisonment, which lasted five days. If I could have seen my mother alone, I should have gone down on my knees to her and besought her forgiveness; but I saw no one, Miss Murdstone excepted, during the whole time—except at evening prayers in the parlour; to which I was escorted by Miss Murdstone after everybody else was placed; where I was stationed, a young outlaw, all alone by myself near the door; and whence I was solemnly conducted by my jailer, before any one arose from the devotional posture.
